James —

Thanks — great constructive back-and-forth. Per our calls and internal review I'm proposing the following compromise for the redline we will send to you formally this afternoon: 

1) Governing Law: The Agreement will be governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

2) Dispute Resolution: Except for injunctive or other provisional relief as set out below, all disputes seeking monetary damages will be resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS. We propose the seat of arbitration to be Boston, Massachusetts. Individual claims under $200,000 may proceed in small claims or similar fora as applicable.

3) Injunctive / Interim Relief Carveout: Either party may seek injunctive or provisional relief in the state or federal courts located in Massachusetts without first submitting the dispute to arbitration where such relief is necessary to prevent irreparable harm, protect customer data, or preserve the status quo pending resolution of the dispute. The party seeking such relief must:
   - Provide written notice to the other party describing the specific emergency and the relief requested;
   - Demonstrate with reasonable particularity why arbitration cannot provide adequate interim relief; and
   - Use best efforts to limit any requested emergency relief to the minimum scope and duration necessary.

4) Expedited Process & Meet-and-Confer: For non-emergency interim requests the parties agree to a 10-business-day meet-and-confer and optional expedited arbitration window prior to filing in court. Emergency filings are permitted without meet-and-confer.

5) Mutuality & Forum Non-Exclusive Motion: The carveout is reciprocal. Proceedings in Massachusetts for interim relief will not prejudice the arbitrator's jurisdiction over the underlying dispute.

Legal-ops, please add this to the deal record and hold the DocuSign envelope until we confirm the final Order Form language. James — if you can confirm Sunrise is okay with Boston as the seat for arbitration and the language above, we'll circulate the final redline and aim to have procurement sign-off by the end of the week.

Appreciate the pragmatic approach — this should keep the sales timeline intact while preserving both parties' urgent-remedy options.
